candidates.why: Official Journal PDF of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act). Producer chain new to the corpus: PDFlib+PDI 9.0.7p3 written by Servigistics Arbortext Publishing Engine -- neither string has appeared in any fixture. EU reuse policy: Commission Decision 2011/833/EU authorises reuse under CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise noted; the notice is site-level rather than printed in this PDF, recorded here as the weaker basis.

Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo (2024), 114 pages. US Supreme Court opinion: a work of the US courts, no copyright claim asserted anywhere in the document. Producer chain new to the corpus: Acrobat Distiller 23.0 from PScript5.dll PostScript -- Word printed to PostScript then distilled, deliberately distinct from the existing Acrobat PDFMaker-for-Word chain (no PDFMaker library involved).

Typst 0.13.1 output, 5 pages. The only verified Typst specimen found; a producer chain no other fixture carries. Host serves it as application/octet-stream but the bytes are a real PDF. MIT licence read from the repository's LICENSE file.

World Development Report 2024 overview booklet, 48 pages. Producer chain new to the corpus: Adobe InDesign 15.1 (Macintosh) through Adobe PDF Library 15.0 / PDF Tools 4.7.24.2 -- professional publishing layout, not a word processor. World Bank Open Knowledge Repository policy: CC BY 3.0 IGO. Host requires GET; HEAD returns 404. Citation basis recorded as repository policy rather than an in-document statement.

The Not So Short Introduction to LaTeX (v6.4), 153 pages. Engine chain new to the corpus: XeLaTeX via xdvipdfmx -- every existing TeX fixture is pdfTeX. GPL statement printed on p.2 of the document itself, quoted at fetch. CTAN mirrors 307-redirect; redirects followed.

LuaTeX 1.24 reference manual, 328 pages, ConTeXt MkIV typeset. Two chains new to the corpus: the LuaTeX engine itself and ConTeXt as the macro package (all existing TeX fixtures are LaTeX). GPL stated on the CTAN luatex package page.

The pandoc MANUAL, 180 pages, produced by pandoc's own LaTeX template through LuaTeX 1.21. The pandoc-to-LaTeX chain is named in the Creator string ('LaTeX via pandoc'); pandoc is among the most common real-world document pipelines. GPL from the pandoc repository COPYING; no in-document statement (checked).

TeX by Topic (Eijkhout), 317 pages, pdfeTeX-1.21a -- a vintage eTeX-era producer string, older than every TeX engine the corpus holds. FDL 1.2 permission statement printed on p.2 of the document itself, quoted at fetch.

GNU Bash Reference Manual, Edition 5.3, 214 pages, pdfTeX 1.40.26 from texinfo via texi2dvi -- the texinfo toolchain is a Creator string ('TeX') no other fixture carries. FDL 1.3 statement printed on p.2 of the document itself, quoted at fetch.

RFC 9000 (QUIC v1), 151 pages, cairo 1.16.0 via xml2rfc 3.8.0 -- the same chain as y17_rfc9110, held as a second specimen because the corpus's 'other real-world' class is 1 of a target 6. IETF Trust TLP section 5.a permits verbatim redistribution of unmodified copies; the frozen-fixture constraint this corpus already imposes is exactly what the TLP requires. Not public domain -- the same recorded caveat as y17.
